You are making ONE surgical fix in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth engines only, zero API spend. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp on every python call. Files you may change: server/pipeline/angle_render.py and tests/test_angle_render.py. Nothing else. Do not touch scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh.

MEASURED FINDING (2026-07-24, receipts in /home/ankit114/ringer-work/podcast-full-auto-muxvariant/mux-truncation-variants/): the program-audio mux in render_angle_switch loses REAL audio. For a 3-segment contiguous 10s program (source 930.0-932.5, 932.5-937.5, 937.5-940.0 off episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4, crossfade_s=0.0) the one-pass filter emits EXACTLY 480,000 PCM samples, but the muxed file decodes to 477,184 -- a 2,816-sample (58.7ms) deficit that survives into the final render. The cause is `-shortest` in the mux command: it terminates the mux before the AAC encoder drains its delayed tail. Packet-level evidence: the baseline writes 467 AAC packets ending at PTS 9.960000; without -shortest the encoder also writes packets at 9.981333, 10.002667 and 10.024000 -- 3 extra packets = 3,072 samples, of which 256 are legitimate terminal padding, leaving exactly the 2,816 that were being lost.

MEASURED VARIANTS (all built and probed, do not re-litigate them):
  current_baseline (with -shortest): 477,184 decoded, delta -2,816.
  no_shortest: 480,256 decoded, delta +256 (inside the AAC-padding-only allowance).
  pcm_intermediate WITH -shortest: still short (-1,792) -- so -shortest, not the AAC encode, is the culprit.
  pcm_intermediate + no_shortest: correct, but costs ~312MB extra per 31-minute program.
  aac + apad + -shortest: still -2,816.
  no_shortest on a second, ~60s multi-segment case: delta +512, i.e. correct at a different length.

THE FIX: delete ONLY the "-shortest" element from the program-audio mux command list in render_angle_switch (server/pipeline/angle_render.py, in the mux_cmd around line 936, currently ending `"-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "aac", "-b:a", "192k", "-ar", "48000", "-ac", "2", "-shortest", muxed`). Leave every other flag alone. Then:
  * Update the surrounding comments (including the render_angle_switch docstring's MUX bullet, around line 805, and the mux comment block around lines 924-925) so they state that -shortest was REMOVED because it truncated the AAC encoder's drained tail, and that the streams match by construction so nothing needs capping. Cite the measured numbers (480,000 filtered / 477,184 with -shortest / 480,256 without).
  * Update the command-contract assertions in tests/test_angle_render.py that currently REQUIRE -shortest (approximately lines 165, 466, 493 and 634-636 -- find them all with grep) so they assert the program mux does NOT use -shortest. Do not simply delete those assertions: invert them, so a future reintroduction of -shortest fails the suite.

ADD tests/test_angle_render.py::test_render_angle_switch_multisegment_preserves_tail_samples. It must build a SYNTHETIC 10-second 30fps source with a continuous 997Hz 48kHz stereo tone that runs to the very end (ffmpeg lavfi is fine -- do not depend on the real episode media, which is not in git), render the three contiguous spans [0,2.5], [2.5,7.5], [7.5,10.0] through the REAL render_angle_switch with crossfade_s=0.0 and a small target_size such as (160,90), read map_total from the emitted .boundaries.json sidecar, sum decoded frame nb_samples, and assert BOTH: (a) the render returns the output path, and (b) 0 <= decoded_samples - round(map_total*48000) <= 1023. It must ALSO prove the tail is real audio and not silence: decode the final to s16le and assert the RMS over the last 2,816 sample-frames is comparable to the RMS of the tone elsewhere in the program (a silence-filled tail must fail this test). Keep the test fast; skip cleanly if ffmpeg is unavailable, exactly like the other executed tests in that file do.

DO NOT touch the audio certification block (the 0..1023 decoded-sample invariant). It is correct and it is what caught this defect. If your change would require loosening it, the change is wrong.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real output into your final message:
  cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_angle_render.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
plus a REAL render of the 3-segment 930.0-940.0 control off episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4 through render_angle_switch (scratch script in YOUR task directory, output in YOUR task directory, never in the episode folder) printing the returned path and the decoded sample count. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
